value.messages: ["Nights 1-3: the 3am wake is the target, so keep everything about it boring. When he wakes, wait a minute or two before you go in - toddlers often resettle if you don't rush. If he's truly up, go in, keep the lights off, no picking up, no talking beyond a few flat words like it's sleep time, and leave while he's still awake. Expect him to protest hard the first couple of nights. That's the pattern shifting, not you doing it wrong.","Nights 4-7: same script every single time, and stretch your wait before going in a little - a couple of minutes longer than before. If he's landing at 3am like clockwork, check the easy culprits: too warm, too light at dawn, a nap running late or long, or a bedtime that's drifted early enough that 3am is genuinely enough sleep for him. Shift bedtime 15 minutes and hold his nap to mid-afternoon. Expect one worse night in here - that's normal, not a relapse.","After that: most families see the 3am wake shrink to a brief stir or disappear in one to two weeks once the response is the same every time. You'll know it's working when he goes back down faster and needs you less. If he's still fully waking every night after two weeks, or the waking comes with pain, fever, or hard breathing, that's worth raising with your doctor rather than riding out."]}
